After having had such a terrific experience with the Dan Henry 1939 model, buying another Henry watch was a very easy decision to make. After all, for a mere $220, the 1939 has leap-frogged its way to becoming a favourite.

Here are the specs for the Dan Henry model 1963:

CASE

  • 42.5mm stainless steel 316L
  • 22mm lugs size
  • 50mm lug to lug
  • Stainless steel 12-hour rotating bezel with 5-min click
  • Screw-back case with Lockheed Blackbird 3D medal
  • Sapphire coated double domed mineral glass with Anti-Reflective treatment

MOVEMENT

  • Miyota 6S20 quartz (Japan) chronograph with smooth motion center seconds. Watch seconds, 60-min and decimal subdials

DIAL

  • Sandwich dial with patina Swiss lumens and silver subdials 60-min chrono subdial at 9 position and 1/10 seconds big subdial at 3 position

The watch arrives in a plastic tube that belies its contents. For $230, you get a 3-watch canvas and leather roll that is of excellent quality.

Inside of said roll is the watch itself, a 1-year warranty card and a black military-grade NATO strap.

The Dan Henry 1963 offers you a choice of two bezels. One is black, to match the dial, and the other is brushed aluminum with the numbers and markers painted black.

I chose the latter, as I feel that the contrast is not only more visually appealing, but it also seems to make the watch wear a bit smaller.

The dial of the Dan Henry 1963, while basically designed by Heuer (Carrera ref. 2447) is a delight in its own right. It is a sandwich-dial, of which I am a fan, that gives nice depth to the Arabic "12" and the baton cut-outs (which are amazingly precise for a watch of this price).

The subdials are as follows:

  • An oversized 1/20th sec. at 3 o'clock (again, thanks Heuer)
  • Running secs. at 6 o'clock
  • Chrono minutes at 9 o'clock

All three are silver (gives a nice panda effect) and are very subtly ringed with concentric circles.

All of the hands that tick line-up with the tic-marks perfectly (quartz watches that don't do this annoy me).

The hands are pencil-style, and are lumed with the brownish-"aged" lume that is overused these days, but I like it on this watch (as I do on a few Steinhart models).

The chrono seconds-hand has a diamond-shaped tip that is lumed, as well.

The case is absolutely the star of the show, here. A lovely mix of polished and brushed (done so well that I can hardly believe the price of this watch), it also has a terrific beveled-and-polished edge on the outside of the lugs that give this piece a lot of class. So nice and well-done. The case-back (Dan Henry obviously loves to do a nice case-back, go and look at his site) is stamped with the outline of my favourite airplane of all-time, the Lockheed SR-71. It also has the number of this "limited-edition" watch (I got 0034/1963).

The buttons operating the Miyota quartz movement are very nice. Oversized and they give a very reassuring "click" every time you press them. I dislike mushy chrono buttons a great deal, but I certainly do not have to worry about that here. Nicely done. The signed "DH" crown is also a very nice touch not seen on a lot of budget watches.

The 1963 comes on a beautiful, hand-sewn Italian leather strap that smells as good as it looks. It is not as immediately comfortable as the band that comes on the 1939, but breaking it in will be a pleasure.

The crystal is a double-domed sapphire-coated mineral type, and it provides lovely distortion when looked at from an angle. My two Dan Henry's are the only watches that I have that have this type of crystal, and I look forward to seeing how durable they might be.

No watch, however, is perfect (except maybe the ROLEX 114060), so here are my complaints:

  • The lume is terrible. I mean just fucking awful.
  • The 12-click bezel (while beautifully machined) could have better resistance and a more reassuring "click."

That's it. Those are my only complaints.

Dan Henry is busily impressing the hell out of me. The product that he delivers for the price is astonishing. My next four watch-purchases are going to be from him (I like every model he offers).

I could not more emphatically recommend Dan Henry wristwatches if I were being paid to do it (which I'm not!).

Look over his offerings and buy the hell out of the one(s) that you like, you will most certainly not regret it.
